name: CelesTrak Reference Nodes
description: Request-builder and parser flow nodes for the CelesTrak reference lanes (typed contracts 1.0: FlatBuffers only, no JSON and no base64). gp_groups turns a TimerTick into one HttpRequest per GP group query (47 GROUP tokens plus the gpz / gpz-plus SPECIAL queries, overridable via node CONFIG celestrak_gp_groups, at most 63), each carrying its job in CONTEXT; parse_gp_groups pairs the groups' HttpResponses with the group plan by the job each carries (any order), resolving the plan from its own node CONFIG exactly as gp_groups does, refuses a partial or foreign set (group-count-mismatch, group-url-mismatch) and emits one $EGP (Entity Group, QUERY_SNAPSHOT membership over the group's OMM rows) per group in plan order, with the concatenated payloads as the raw archive (one HttpResponse naming the elements index) and a FlowNotice Unchanged for groups that answered 304. satcat_reference emits the launch-site and owner/source table fetches; parse_satcat_reference reads those HTML tables into $SIT rows (launch sites) or $LCC rows (legacy owner codes, matched strictly against the generated enum; unknown codes become provenance warnings and are skipped), deciding by the job's DATASET_ID. JOB STATE TRAVELS AS HttpRequest.CONTEXT: one size-prefixed $ICN (Ingest Connector) record naming the lane - CONNECTOR_ID (the source name; a GP group: celestrak-gp-groups/<TOKEN>), ENDPOINT_URL, TARGET_SCHEMA, EMITS_SCHEMAS, ORIGIN_ID celestrak.org, ORIGIN_NAME CelesTrak, DATASET_ID, PROVIDER_ID, SOURCE_NAME and the usage terms LICENSE / LICENSE_URL / CITATION (node CONFIG celestrak_provider_id / celestrak_license / celestrak_license_url / celestrak_citation override the defaults) - echoed by hostcap/http-request. Every ingest meta is an IngestRequest (SourceTags attribution, RECONCILE, ARCHIVE celestrak/<the lane's archive name, keyed by DATASET_ID>, PROVENANCE); TAGS.LICENSE is an SPDX identifier, so prose terms are named LicenseRef-CelesTrak-Usage-Policy there (the verbatim text stays in the job and in each $EGP's PROVENANCE.LICENSE). Node CONFIG through plugin.getConfig (SDS $PIV, one ModuleConfig FlatBuffer). No capabilities: plugin.getConfig is a builtin and this module performs no I/O of its own.

sequentialJustification.detail: Every method is a single pass over the frames of one invocation: the request builders read the node config once and emit request frames; the parsers decode each response once into records. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool and no fan-out inside the guest; the fan-out across group queries is the flow's, through the http connector node. This guest can never spawn a thread, so it compiles wasi-sequential rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: The groups' HttpResponses -> one $EGP per group. Each response names its group by its $ICN job's CONNECTOR_ID (celestrak-gp-groups/<TOKEN>); the group plan is resolved from node CONFIG (celestrak_gp_groups) exactly as gp_groups resolves it. The batch is refused (group-count-mismatch) unless exactly one response per planned group arrived and (group-url-mismatch) for a group outside the plan or a URL other than the plan's; a response without an $ICN job is refused (missing-context). A group answering 304 is reported on 'unchanged'; any other non-200 status fails the batch, matching the CelesTrak usage policy. Records, the batch id (sha256 of the concatenated payloads) and the raw archive follow plan order. Each $EGP carries GROUP_ID celestrak.org/gp/<token>, sorted and deduplicated TAGS, QUERY_SNAPSHOT membership with one member per OMM row ($OMM, OBJECT_ID, NORAD_CAT_ID), the query URL, and provenance with the group payload's sha256 and the licence terms. Reconcile Current for a complete snapshot, Duplicates when some groups answered 304. node CONFIG celestrak_gp_groups_emit_omm re-emits the group rows as $OMM.

methods.description: HttpResponse -> scans the page's first HTML table (tags stripped, entities decoded) and emits $SIT rows (ID and ABBREVIATION = the code, NAME and DESCRIPTION = the table description, SITE_TYPE LAUNCH_SITE, SOURCE CelesTrak) when the $ICN job's DATASET_ID is satcat-launch-sites, or $LCC rows (OWNER matched exactly against the generated legacyCountryCode labels, NAME/DESCRIPTION, ACTIVE, SOURCE_URL, RETRIEVED_AT from the response Date header) when it is satcat-owners; any other dataset is refused (unknown-reference-dataset). An owner code absent from the enum is recorded as a provenance warning and skipped, never remapped. 304 emits only a FlowNotice on 'unchanged'. The input port is single-stream; a surplus is refused (batched-input-frames).
